subject: Private connectivity & SDK integration — post-discovery checklist
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Saunders <emily.saunders@veridianlabs.com>, Marcus Holt <cto@veridianlabs.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Private connectivity & SDK integration — post-discovery checklist

Hi Emily / Marcus,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Below is a concise recap + proposed next steps so both teams can align on the network and integration requirements before the technical POC. I attached a one-page mutual action plan and the infra sketch.

Top-line ask from Veridian: production-grade private connectivity + controlled egress for PHI-bound inference traffic, and a simple SDK path for devs to call Redwood with structured output + tool-calling enabled.

Recap & open items (action owners in parentheses):

1) Private connectivity model (Veridian to confirm choice):
   - Option A: AWS PrivateLink (VPC Endpoint Service) to a dedicated Redwood endpoint in us-west-2 (preferred for no cross-account VPC peering). (Emily)
   - Option B: VPC Peering / Transit gateway (if you prefer direct peering for lower latency). (Emily)

2) IP allowlist vs. private endpoint: if you choose PrivateLink, we will need your account CIDR(s) and subnets to create the endpoint service. If you choose allowlist, provide the public egress IP ranges we should expect. (Emily)

3) mTLS & auth model: you wanted certificate-based mutual TLS for session authentication + per-service API keys for RBAC. We typically support client certs for PrivateLink + API key rotation via our Console. Need to confirm cert provisioning flow (bring-your-own cert / Redwood CA). (Marcus Lin)

4) SDK setup + routing: devs will point SDK to a custom base_url (private endpoint). We need to validate that your egress DNS resolves to the PrivateLink CNAME, and discuss split-horizon DNS if applicable. (Lauren)

5) Structured output & tool calling: you plan to rely on function-style structured output for prescribing downstream actions (billing code extraction). We'll document recommended schemas and provide a sample OpenAPI spec and SDK helpers. (Stephanie)

6) Embeddings & rerank: you mentioned hosting your embedding index in your VPC for data locality. Two options: (a) use Redwood embeddings + offboard vectors to your index (we provide vector export hooks), or (b) host embeddings in Redwood Dedicated and use our reranker. Need to decide for POC. (Stephanie)

Proposed next steps:
- Veridian to confirm connectivity option (PrivateLink vs peering) and share the relevant AWS account details & subnet CIDRs (Emily) — target: Tue 2028-05-16
- Redwood infra & SEs (Marcus, Lauren) to produce precise endpoint/cert instructions and a dev SDK snippet for PrivateLink by Wed 2028-05-18
- Set up short 45-min technical POC call (network + auth + SDK) for next week — propose Thu 2028-05-18 10am PT / alternative Fri 11am PT

Attaching: mutual-action-plan-veridian.xlsx, veridian-infra-diagram.png

Thanks — I’ll loop in the right SEs for the technical follow-up once you confirm the connectivity choice.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Emily Saunders <emily.saunders@veridianlabs.com>, Marcus Holt <cto@veridianlabs.com>
Date: Sat, 12 May 2028 08:09:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private connectivity & SDK integration — technical notes (PrivateLink, mTLS, SDK, rerank)

Emily / Marcus (Veridian) — looping in some technical detail ahead of the POC so the meeting can focus on any policy questions and the live demo.

PrivateLink notes:
- We will create a Redwood VPC Endpoint Service in us-west-2. For PrivateLink we need your AWS account ID + two (2) subnets (AZ diversity) and the IDs of the ENIs you'll attach. We will provide the service name (com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xxxxx) that you will use to create the VPC Endpoint in your account.
- DNS: PrivateLink gives you a regional endpoint CNAME. If you use split-horizon DNS, make sure your internal DNS resolves the production FQDN to the VPCE CNAME. If you cannot manage DNS, we can provide a dedicated host name you can put in /etc/hosts for the POC.

mTLS / certs:
- BYO cert is fine. We support client cert validation where clients present an X.509 cert on TCP handshake and we map the cert SAN to a tenant binding for RBAC. We will need the client cert's issuing CA chain (PEM) and the expected subject/SAN format.
- Rotation: recommend short lifecycle (90d). For rotation, Veridian should upload the new cert to our customer Console and kick a validation (we accept a verification call/out-of-band signature). We will also support ACME-style automation if you want it later.

SDK / routing:
- SDKs accept a base_url override and optional client_cert + client_key paths (or an in-memory cert object). Example (Python):

  rdw = Redwood(client_key_path="/opt/certs/veridian.key", client_cert_path="/opt/certs/veridian.crt", base_url="https://private-vrd.redwood.internal")
  resp = rdw.generate(prompt, structured_output=...")

- For function/tool calling we send a JSON-LD response with clear schema. If you want strict validation server-side, we can enable schema enforcement in the POC.

Embeddings & reranker options:
- Short POC path (fastest): Veridian computes embeddings locally; on a query, Veridian sends top-K candidate IDs + their vectors to Redwood reranker endpoint (we accept precomputed vectors in the request body) and Redwood returns scores and re-ranked ids. This avoids vector export during the POC.
- Alternative: store vectors in Redwood Dedicated and call a rerank pipeline there — simpler from our side but means vectors leave your VPC.
- Rate limits: reranker accepting precomputed vectors is rate-limited per-minute; we should size based on expected QPS.

Network security checklist for POC:
- Ports: HTTPS (443) only over PrivateLink; no public egress required for inference traffic.
- DNS: confirm internal DNS resolves the endpoint CNAME.
- ACLs/security groups: allow outbound connections from your compute to the VPCE in the specified subnets.

Deliverables before POC (I'll own the endpoint details doc and SDK snippets):
- Redwood: PrivateLink service name + BYO cert validation process + Python/Node SDK examples (deliver by 2028-05-16).
- Veridian: AWS account ID, two subnet IDs (us-west-2), cert chain PEM for client cert, and an example embedding vector payload shape you expect to send (deliver by 2028-05-16).

If that works, we’ll use the Thu slot to validate cert handshake, DNS resolution, a sample SDK request with structured output enabled, and a reranker call with precomputed vectors.

—Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
